context: Daichi and Tatsuya talk honestly about countryside reality versus city life.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: たつや、この町、人々、減ってる？
lines.en: Tatsuya — the town, the people. They're getting fewer, aren't they?
lines.style: Warm Kansai lilt with genuine concern underneath. Leans in slightly. Asks without pushing. Soft, observant — the cadence of someone who knows this place.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.style: Quiet, measured. Long exhale before speaking. Rural composure — not avoiding the weight, just carrying it steadily. Words spaced like they cost something.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.en: The young people — they're leaving for the city, yeah?
lines.style: Kansai warmth with a note of sadness. Slower pace. Testing whether he's seeing it right. Seeks confirmation, not blame.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.en: Not enough work. There's no other choice.
lines.style: Matter-of-fact but not bitter. Slight shrug in the voice. The acceptance of something understood long ago. Philosophical — not fighting it, just acknowledging.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: 過去の町、覚えてる？賑やかやったやろ。
lines.en: You remember what this town was like before? It was vibrant — everyone out, alive.
lines.style: Nostalgia softens the Kansai warmth. Sits back into memory. The brightness of the past lives in his voice. Inviting Tatsuya to remember with him.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.jp: 昔は、祭り、皆で、楽しんだ。
lines.en: Back then, the festivals — everyone came together. We enjoyed them.
lines.style: Eyes distant. Voice carries the weight of remembering something good that's fading. Slow, tender, like holding a fragile memory. The word 'enjoyed' lingers.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: なんとか、出来へんかな、町のために。
lines.en: There's got to be something we can do. For the town. There just has to be.
lines.style: The Kansai brightness returning — not naive, but searching. Leans forward. Determination softened by genuine care. Turning the corner from loss toward possibility.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.jp: 小さい事から、始めるしかない。
lines.en: We can only start with small things.
lines.style: Not dismissive — grounding. Steady, practical wisdom. The voice of someone who's built things slowly. Open door at the end — inviting, not closing off.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: 皆で、何か、出来そうやな。
lines.en: All of us together — I reckon we could do something real.
lines.style: Kansai warmth brightens. Conviction settling in. Looks directly at Tatsuya. The old friend seeing a path forward. Energy steady, not forced.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.style: Agreement that carries quiet strength. Opens his hand. The words are an invitation — to work together, to believe together. Gentle but clear.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: 次に来る時、案、持ってくるわ。
lines.en: Next time I come, I'll bring some ideas. Real ones.
lines.style: Commitment in the Kansai cadence. Brighter, more energized. A promise being made — not lightly, but with the warmth of friendship. Stands taller in the voice.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.en: That helps. That helps a lot.
lines.style: Gratitude that runs deep but stays quiet. Small words carrying big weight. The exhale of someone who didn't realize he needed help until it was offered. Ends gently.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.en: This town — we're keeping it. No matter what.
lines.style: Final commitment. The Kansai warmth crystallizes into promise. Steady, unshakeable. Eyes on the future. Voice carries the weight of a man standing by his word.
